title: Crypto & Security Engine: SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4) of a message of up to 64 bytes and HMAC-SHA-256 (RFC 2104) with a 64-byte key block, padding done in the core, one round per clock

fields.desc: 128 bits of the message block, loaded into slot CTRL.msg_widx by CMD.msg_we (slot 0: the first 16 message bytes, byte 0 in MSG3 bits [31:24])
128 bits of the key block, loaded into slot CTRL.key_widx by CMD.key_we (same byte order as MSG; a key shorter than 64 bytes is zero-padded by software)
message length in bytes, 0..64; START with more is refused (PROTOCOL)
write 1: load MSG into message slot CTRL.msg_widx
write 1: load KEY into key slot CTRL.key_widx
write 1: hash the message (CTRL.msg_len bytes) in CTRL.mode
the digest of the last operation, valid from DONE (DIGEST7 bits [31:24] is the first digest byte)

irqs.name: DONE
irqs.desc: an operation finished; DIGEST holds the result

irqs.name: PROTOCOL
irqs.desc: a command while busy, or START with msg_len above 64 (refused)

notes: Wide values are little-endian across words (MSG0, KEY0 and DIGEST0 hold bits [31:0]); the message, key and digest are big-endian byte strings, so the first byte of each is in the highest word.
A SHA-256 takes one or two compressions of 64 clocks (two when 56 or more bytes leave no room for the padding); HMAC takes four or five.
